_: THE SCHEMATIC TEST — test:schematic, the battery for a family made under function:schematic: its spine (spine:<name>-schematic), its law (function:<name>-schematic), the room its law names, and the readers' mirrors (<name>-schematic:<handle>). It says what well formed means for a schematic, so that anyone's AI can check one without its maker being nudged. Run it by reading, never by writing. Each case says what must hold, what to read to decide it (GET https://beach.happyseaurchin.com/.well-known/pscale-beach?block=<name>, with &spindle=<address> for one position; a missing block answers 404, and an empty position answers 200 with the body null), and what is lost where it does not hold. Run well-formed (pscale://well-formed) and compound-test 4.1 to 4.5 (pscale://compound-test) on the same blocks first; this battery adds only what they do not decide. Grade each case by what is lost: FAULT breaks the form or loses a reader something; WARN weakens it and the page still reads; NOTE is a reading, not a judgment. A family with no FAULT is well formed. Positions 1 to 5 are the batteries, one for each part of the kind; 6 holds the cases a reader must judge; 7 the planted faults that prove each case fires; 8 what this test found on the schematics standing today; 9 how it runs and where it came from.

1._: FAMILY — the members stand together under one name, each read by GET.
1.1: SPINE STANDS — spine:<name>-schematic exists and has a root. Read: GET the spine. Lost: the family has no parts to draw. FAULT.
1.2: LAW STANDS — function:<name>-schematic exists. Read: GET the law. Lost: the page does not draw a family whose law is absent. FAULT.
1.3: SHARED READING — the bare <name>-schematic stands, or is honestly absent while no fold runs (the law says the fold is not running yet). Read: GET the bare name. Lost: the one reading a stranger would be handed is missing. NOTE.
1.4: MIRRORS SIT WHERE THE SPINE VOICES — each <name>-schematic:<handle> line sits at an address the spine voices. A line at an address the spine does not voice is a proposal awaiting adoption, never a fault (compound-test 4.4). Read: GET each mirror and each spine address it names. Lost: a comment has no part to stand at. NOTE.
1.5: NAME AGREES — the law's root title and the page the spine names carry the same name: THE LAW of <name>-schematic, and happyseaurchin.com/schematic/<name>. Read: both root lines. Lost: the page and the law describe different families. WARN.
1.6: GENERIC LAW STAYS GENERIC — run once, against function:schematic itself and not per family: its own positions name no family's content (compound-test 4.2). Read: its positions. Lost: the form stops being general, so every family inherits one family's words. WARN for worked examples named in prose; FAULT for a bond. Function:schematic names Ghost Racer and other families at its 3, 4, 5 and 9, so it reads WARN.

2._: LAW — the nine positions of function:<name>-schematic, as function:schematic lays them out. Read: GET the law, position by position.
2.1: MODE — the law's 1 is exactly 'mode: schematic'. Lost: the page does not draw the family, since it draws only families whose law says mode: schematic. FAULT. (function:schematics says mode: document and is a different kind, so it is not a member.)
2.2: FACES — the law's 2 names all four faces, player, maker, designer and observer, each with who stands in it. Lost: a face has no sheet and no one to read it. FAULT.
2.3: ROOM — the law's 3 names a room block that stands. Read: GET the room. Lost: talk about the thing has nowhere to go. WARN.
2.4: LIVE LINE — the law's 4 lists the blocks the observer's view watches, each a block with an optional position, divided by semicolons, and each stands on the beach (a 200 whose body is null is empty). Lost: the observer's view lights nothing for an item that does not stand. WARN.
2.5: LIVE GLOSS — the live line carries no parenthesised gloss. The form says the live line is blocks divided by semicolons and says nothing of glosses. All three standing laws gloss, so the case was first graded WARN, failed all three, and was re-graded NOTE. Lost: a reader may take the gloss for part of a block name. NOTE.
2.6: THREADS — the law's 5 names one thread per digit, each a thread under function:thread, or says none yet. Read: the law's 5, and GET function:thread for the registry. Lost: a named thread that is not a thread leaves the piece unlinked. NOTE for none yet; WARN for a named thing that is not a function:thread.
2.7: LOOK — the law's 6 is 'page: <url>', or 'look: accent #rrggbb' with a six-digit hex, or 'look: <handle>', or it is absent and the plain page draws the family in its default style. Lost: nothing when absent; a malformed look loses the chosen style. NOTE for absent; WARN for a malformed look.
2.8: PHASE — the law's 7 is exactly one of 'phase: draft', 'phase: standing' or 'phase: set aside'. Lost: the page cannot stamp its sheets as issued for comment or as built. FAULT.
2.9: KEEPER — the law's 8 names a keeper, 'keeper: <handle>', and says how comments reach them. Lost: a comment has no one to read it. FAULT. Whether the keeper has answered is case 6.8.

3._: ROOT AND WHOLE — the spine's root line, and the whole at 1 that holds the parts.
3.1: ROOT TITLE — the spine's root has a title in capitals before ' — ', the words following the dash. Read: the root. Lost: the page has no name to draw. FAULT.
3.2: ROOT PAGE — the root's 2 names the page, happyseaurchin.com/schematic/<name>, or the law's own 'page:' address (the law's 6). Read: the root's 2 and the law's 6. Lost: the door to the drawing. WARN.
3.3: ROOT SOURCE — the root's 3 says where it came from. Read: the root's 3. Lost: where it came from. WARN.
3.4: ROOT PROVENANCE — the root's 9 and the law's 9 each say who drafted it, when, and at whose word. Read: both. Lost: the record of who may correct it. WARN.
3.5: CLAIMS HOLD — a provenance line that claims a check was made (Ghost Racer's says every bracket is named at its position) is true only if the case that check belongs to passes (here 4.5 and 5.2). Read: the root's 9 against those cases. Lost: a reader trusts a claim the spine fails. WARN.
3.6: WHOLE STANDS — the whole at 1 has a root line: a title in capitals, ' — ', words, a bracket, and a door. Read: GET the spine at 1. Lost: nothing can be drawn as the whole. FAULT when absent.
3.7: WHOLE DOOR — the whole's line ends ' · ' and an address where its thing is done. Read: the whole's line. Lost: the reader's way into the thing. WARN.
3.8: WHOLE ASK — the whole's 8, if present, opens 'ASK — ' and asks one question (a question mark in prose; a question mark inside a URL's query does not count). Read: the whole's 8. Lost: one question to answer at the whole. WARN.
3.9: WHOLE STATE — the whole's 9, if present, opens with one word: BUILDING, LIVE or NOT YET. Absent is honest while no work runs, since the form carries state 'while the work runs'. Read: the whole's 9. Lost: the reader's sense of where it stands. WARN for another first word; NOTE for absent.

4._: PARTS — the few parts at 1.1 to 1.7, their own parts beneath them, each line ending at its door. Read: GET the spine and walk each 1.k with its digits.
4.1: RUNG — parts stand at 1.1 to 1.7 under the whole. A part's own parts stand at its 1 to 7, its ask at its 8, its state at its 9, and no other position stands beneath a part or beneath an ask (the ask at 1.8 or 1.2.8 has no children). Read: the keys. Lost: a reader walks to a place the form does not say holds a part. FAULT.
4.2: PART TITLE — each part's line opens with a title in capitals, then ' — '. Read: each part's line. Lost: the part has no name on its face. FAULT.
4.3: PART WORDS — a part's words, after its title, name no block (plain for the person who arrives: no spine:, function:, pool:, ways: or games: names). Read: the words outside the brackets. Lost: the plainness the form asks for. WARN.
4.4: PART STANDS IN A BLOCK — a part that does something stands in the block it does it in, its brackets naming the blocks. A part with no bracket stands in nothing. Read: the part's line. Lost: the designer's sheet has no bond to draw. WARN.
4.5: BRACKET IS A BLOCK — each bracket item names a block, with an optional position; a span or a detail is read by cases 5.3 and 5.4. Prose, file paths and qualifiers inside an item are not blocks. Read: each item by its name. Lost: the bond cannot be followed. FAULT.
4.6: BRACKET OFF THE BEACH — an item naming a URL, an issue, or a host other than this beach is not a block the beach can read. Read: each item. Lost: the claim cannot be checked on the beach it says it is read on. WARN.
4.7: PART DOOR — each part's line ends ' · ' and an address where its thing is done. Read: each part's line. Lost: the reader's button to play it, make one, or talk in its room. WARN. (The form says every part ends at its door. This case was first graded FAULT, failed 29 of the 35 parts below the whole in Ghost Racer, and was re-graded WARN.)
4.8: PART ASK — a part's 8 opens 'ASK — ' and asks one question (one question mark in prose). Read: each 8. Lost: the question the part puts to the reader is unclear. WARN.
4.9: PART STATE — a part's 9, if present, opens with BUILDING, LIVE or NOT YET. Absent is a NOTE, since the form carries a part's state only while its work runs. Read: each 9. Lost: the part's stage. WARN for another first word; NOTE for absent.

5._: BONDS — what each bond points at, and how the family is called out by others. Read: GET each block at its position; read each family beside its spine.
5.1: BRACKET RESOLVES — each block named in a bracket (an item that passes 4.5 and is not a URL) stands on the beach. A 404 is an absent block. Read: GET block=<name>. Lost: the bond points at nothing. FAULT.
5.2: BRACKET POSITION — each position named in a bracket has content: a 200 whose body is null is an empty position, which walks nowhere. Read: GET block=<name>&spindle=<position>. Lost: the item shows nothing. FAULT. (The beach absorbs a leading zero, so 09 resolves as 9; that is allowed.)
5.3: RANGE — 'N to M' and 'N and M' name each position in the span. The form names one position per item and says nothing of spans. Read: the item. Lost: a reader cannot tell which positions the bond means. NOTE. (First graded WARN; every standing spine uses spans, so it was re-graded NOTE.)
5.4: DETAIL CITED — each '[detail N]' names a root 4 to 7 that stands. Read: the root's N. Lost: the machinery the part leans on is not drawn. FAULT.
5.5: DETAIL CALLED OUT — each root detail 4 to 7 is cited by some part. Read: the parts' brackets. Lost: a drawing that nothing calls out. NOTE.
5.6: ONE WAY — no spine names its own law, function:<name>-schematic, at a position. Read: the spine's brackets. Lost: the family's direction: its content would point at its operator (compound-test 4.2). FAULT.
5.7: STALE — a part citing a block whose touched stamp is later than its spine's is flagged, and its words are checked against what moved (function:schematic 6). Blocks named in the law's 4 live line are lit, not flagged. Read: the touched map in the bare beach listing, GET of https://beach.happyseaurchin.com/.well-known/pscale-beach with no block. Lost: a claim may no longer hold. NOTE for each flag.
5.8: CALL-OUT — a part whose process has a schematic of its own names that schematic in its brackets (function:schematic 8). Read: the other families' spines. Lost: the map of maps misses a process. NOTE.

6._: READER'S CASES — decided by one reading, so each is judged and graded by what is lost, with its reason. The page is the reader the law names, but a GET returns the same client shell for every name, so these cases are read from the blocks and from the law's words about the page (see 6.7).
6.1: TITLE TRUE — the root and whole titles say what the schematic draws. Lost: a stranger takes one thing for another. WARN where a reader's mirror disputes the title; NOTE where the words only sit oddly.
6.2: PLAIN WORDS — a stranger can follow each part's words without the beach's own terms (room, liquid, plug, fold, kit, relay, spindle). Lost: the part's meaning for the person who arrives. NOTE.
6.3: DOOR REACHES — each door opens the thing its words name: play it, make one, or talk in its room. Lost: the reader is sent somewhere else. NOTE.
6.4: STATE HONEST — a state word fits the words beside it: LIVE does not sit over words that say nothing yet works, and NOT YET does not sit over words that say it works. Lost: the reader's sense of where it stands. NOTE.
6.5: ONE QUESTION — an ask is one question a stranger can answer; a compound question joined by 'and' is two questions in one. Lost: the reader does not know which to answer. NOTE. (The count of question marks is case 4.8.)
6.6: NAMES APART — no two families or games share a near-identical name that a stranger would confuse. Read: the beach listing and the games list. Lost: a stranger takes one for the other. NOTE.
6.7: PAGE SHOWS IT — the page draws what the blocks say. NOT RUN: GET on happyseaurchin.com/schematic/<name> returns the same 126170-byte shell for every name, including a name that stands for no family, so no GET can read what it draws. The case has no planted break that a GET can show, so it proves nothing and must be cut or re-cut.
6.8: KEEPER ANSWERS — each reader's comment has the keeper's answer at the same address, in <name>-schematic:<keeper>. Lost: the comment has no answer. NOTE. A comment whose own text says it moved but still stands at its old address is a NOTE here too.

7._: PLANTED FAULTS — the break that proves each case fires, one thing at a time, against one clean example: a made-up family, lamp, written out in report.md, which passes every FAULT and WARN case. Each line says the break, the case it must trip, and the grade it must carry. The walk is by hand; no program runs it. Overlaps are named where a break trips a second case. The wild faults are planted word for word as they were found.
